raj: Heads-up — seeing OOM spikes on dedicated GPUs when batch_size=8 + seq_len=4096. FlashAttention sometimes falls back to cuBLASLt and we end up OOMing. Anyone seen this pattern?

emma: Yep, saw it on canary yesterday. FFN workspace seems to explode >1.2GB for some shapes and the allocator won't compact, so fragmentation causes OOM even when free memory exists. cc @sophia

infra-bot: perfbot: started profile 1775123460 for job=canary-ffn-4096, collecting nvprof and tracer logs.

sophia: Quick summary from the profile: FlashAttention picks LA=256 for those shapes which increases its temp workspace. Then Triton planner requests cuBLASLt matmul workspace ~800MB for the FFN path. Combined with KV cache buffers we cross device memory. Two prongs: 1) cap per-kernel workspace via selector heuristics and 2) reuse KV/prefix buffers between concurrent streams.

raj: sample nvidia-smi snippet from the run:
```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
| Fan  Temp  Perf  Pwr:Usage/Cap| Memory-Usage | GPU-Util      
| 0   A100  On       00000000:00:1E.0  Off |   48338MiB / 81920MiB |   98%  
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Processes:                                                                  |
|   python (pid 1234)   42000MiB                                               |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
We had ~32GB free but allocation failed due to fragmentation when Triton asked for a single large workspace.

emma: I ran a microbench sweep (seq_len 512 -> 4096). Observed a knee at 2048 where FlashAttention's temp > cuBLASLt's workspace. At 4096 combined peak hits ~55GB across two GPUs with batch pooling. I'll prototype a per-model workspace_hint that forces FlashAttention to pick LA smaller for high-seq tails.

sophia: Allocator tweak that helped in dev: reduce max_small_alloc to 32MB and enable best-fit fallback. That reduced fragmentation; allocator stats showed ~2.1GB free but split into small blocks before the change. Also adding a reclaim-on-fallback path (free unused KV buffers when a kernel fallback path is triggered) helped.

raj: For KV cache reuse: we should attach a small header to the request context so multiple requests on the same session can reuse prefix KV buffers. Lifetime tracking must be robust (evict on LRU or on-request-complete). This would avoid allocating new large KV chunks for each inflight request.

emma: Proposed short-term plan: 1) add soft cap 512MB per-kernel workspace in the selector; if exceeded, force streaming attention fallback. 2) Enable allocator best-fit and lower small-alloc threshold in runtime config. 3) Reuse KV buffers across streams where lifetime allows. Long-term: autotuner that picks LA/block sizes based on seq-length histograms + a defrag pass in the allocator.

sophia: I'll open an RFC and a small canary flag for the selector cap and allocator config. If we ship the cap behind a flag we can monitor perf delta. Anyone object to a quick canary today? :thumbsup:

raj: :thumbsup:
